newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen Development Bank suspended.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen Development Bank suspended.

text.p: Trading in Shenzhen Development Bank shares was suspended on Monday afternoon by the Shenzhen stock exchange after volatile price movements last Friday and this morning, brokers said.

Brokers said they received a notice from the Shenzhen Stock Exchange just before the afternoon session saying trading in the bank's shares would be suspended in the afternoon because of volatile price movements.
Exchange officials could not be immediately reached for comment.
Trading in the shares resumed last Friday after a five-session suspension as punishment for share trading irregularities.
The bank closed up 10 percent last Friday due in part to investor optimism over the bank's earnings outlook, brokers have said.

The bank, an A share market leader with large capitalisation and solid earnings record, extended gains into this morning and closed the session up 7.77 percent at 36.60 yuan on volume of 28 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.
Earlier this month, Beijing securities authorities announced it would sack the bank's president He Yun after the bank was found to have used bank funds to trade its own shares.
Beijing also said it would confiscate nearly 100 million yuan in profits from its illegal stock trading.

Shenzhen Development Bank, China's only bank with a domestic exchange listing, led a bull-run in Shenzhen's A share market between January and May this year before giving up some gains because of official investigations into its share trading. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
